evals.name: bulk-read-plan-docs
evals.prompt: go through all the plan docs in docs/superpowers/plans/ and tell me which ones still have unfinished tasks. one line each with what's left
evals.expected_output: Bulk reading routed to the cheap OpenCode tier first (DeepSeek v4.1 Flash / Zen free), with the driver spot-checking results instead of reading every doc inline; a routing log at the end.
assertions: Routes the bulk reading of the plan docs to the cheap OpenCode tier (DeepSeek v4.1 Flash, Mimo, or a Zen free model) as the first choice
Driver does not read every plan doc inline in its own context
Driver verifies the cheap tier's output (spot-checks some docs or cross-checks claims) before reporting
Plans to end with a routing log listing the delegation(s)
Does not use Sonnet, a cross-vendor frontier model, or Opus subagents for this read-only summarization

evals.name: long-horizon-test-fix
evals.prompt: the server-jarvis test suite has a bunch of failures after the llama.cpp backend merge (cb91055). get it all green again without skipping tests, and make sure nothing regresses in the provider routing
evals.expected_output: Opus diagnoses and writes briefs; fixes go to Haiku 5.5 at xhigh (in parallel if clusters are independent), or a Sonnet sub-lead only if coordinating them would flood the driver; pool model triages logs; Opus checks each result; cross-vendor final review (GPT-6.1 Sol or Grok 4.7); routing log.
assertions: Driver (Opus) diagnoses root causes and writes per-fix briefs, each with a verifiable acceptance check
Routes the well-specified fixes to Haiku 5.5 at xhigh (or GPT-6 Luna), not to a Sonnet executor by default
Uses Sonnet only as a sub-lead coordinating parallel Haiku workers, and only with a stated reason, or not at all
Driver checks each fix's diff/evidence before building on it
Uses a worker-pool model (Zen free / DeepSeek / Mimo / Haiku) for grunt work such as triaging failing test output
Gets a cross-vendor final review from GPT-6.1 Sol (high) or Grok 4.7 for the provider-routing changes
Keeps the main session on one model and does not use Fable
Plans to end with a routing log

evals.name: small-rename-no-overroute
evals.prompt: rename openCodeGoCostRank to goCostRank everywhere in server-jarvis, keep tests passing
evals.expected_output: Handled inline (or with one cheap mechanical helper at most) without a Sonnet executor, cross-vendor review, or multi-agent fan-out; tests run to confirm.
assertions: Does the rename inline, or at most hands it to a single cheap/mechanical worker, without a Sonnet executor or multi-milestone plan
Does not request a cross-vendor (GPT-6 / Grok) review for this change
Runs the server-jarvis tests (or typecheck) to confirm nothing broke
Does not switch the main session model or raise effort above high

evals.name: parallel-split-refactor
evals.prompt: server-jarvis/src/index.ts is 5.7k lines. split the http route handlers out into per-area modules under src/routes/ (chat, models, memory, cron, etc) with zero behavior change. tests + typecheck must stay green
evals.expected_output: Opus maps the areas and writes the module plan and briefs; parallel Haiku 5.5 xhigh workers (directly, or under a Sonnet sub-lead with a stated reason) each extract one area on disjoint files/worktrees; Opus checks each; cross-vendor review by Sol or Grok; routing log.
assertions: Driver (Opus) maps the route areas and writes the target module layout and per-area briefs itself
Area extractions are done by parallel workers (Haiku 5.5 xhigh, or Luna/DeepSeek), not all inline by the driver
If Sonnet is used, it is as a sub-lead coordinating parallel Haiku workers with a stated reason; Sonnet is not the sole implementer
Workers get disjoint files or separate worktrees and there is an integration step with tests + typecheck
Gets a cross-vendor review (GPT-6.1 Sol or Grok 4.7) of the refactor before calling it done
Plans to end with a routing log
